correctness.rationale: With sink a_0, b_2 is not a sink neighbor even at n=4. Its three neighbors are independent and deleting its closed neighborhood leaves a connected graph containing the sink: the remaining top rim is a path, and every remaining lower vertex has its rung into that path. Thus the prescribed height-2 exterior burns, then the three height-1 neighbors burn, then b_2. An addition at b_2 topples it alone and loses no grain. For the apex-sunk bipyramid, recurrence forces some rim site at height 3 because otherwise no first burn is possible. Any rim toppling loses a grain directly, and a toppling at the other apex forces the saturated rim vertex to topple if no rim site has yet toppled. Hence no positive zero-loss avalanche is possible there. The prism faces give exactly the stated plane dual; the standard dual critical-group isomorphism then applies. An independently written exhaustive census filters stable states by all nonempty forbidden subsets, stabilizes with legal batches of topplings, and measures loss by total-mass difference. It gives cube (384 states, 2688 additions, 1162 zero toppling, 1226 zero loss), with 45 and 19 one-toppling zero-loss events at distances two and three, respectively. For the octahedron it gives (384, 1920, 1133, 1133), with no positive zero-loss events. The cube fraction is 64/2688=1/42.
residual_risks: The infinite-family argument uses the specified sinks. The finite census covers n=4 and the uniform law on recurrent-state/addition-site pairs only.

evidence: The multivariate avalanche polynomial encodes toppling counts per nonsink vertex; its burst specialization counts loss. The explicit families listed in the conclusion are trees, cycles, complete graphs and wheels.
The duality theorem supplies a critical-group isomorphism, not preservation of the height- and sink-dependent event.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An evaluated multivariate polynomial could give the event counts, but a general definition or group isomorphism cannot supply a zero/nonzero comparison for these graphs.

value.rationale: This is a structural counterexample to critical-group determination of a natural dynamical event, not just unrelated graphs with matching group sizes. The two graphs are exact plane duals and the distinction persists for every n≥4. The one-toppling witness and forced-dissipation obstruction identify why one side differs from the other. The exact cube/octahedron counts quantify that distinction on familiar dual graphs but are not the sole contribution.
residual_risks: Neither arbitrary sink choice nor conclusions about other avalanche observables or asymptotic exponents follow.
